images.prompt: A quiet path through an old grove of wild camellia trees at the last of the winter dusk. The grove is an old wood of wild Japanese camellia trees (yabu-tsubaki, Camellia japonica) on a quiet hillside in Japan: smooth pale grey trunks, dense dark glossy evergreen leaves, and single deep-red five-petalled flowers, each with a short cup of golden stamens, not roses, not peonies, not double flowers. A narrow earthen path covered in soft green moss winds through the grove, and whole fallen camellia flowers lie face-up on the moss, still perfectly red and intact. The trees close in on both sides and overhead, which fills the background and shuts out any further view: no distant mountains, no sea, no lake, no far horizon. No buildings, no houses, no temples, no shrines, no torii, no stone lanterns, no lanterns, no bridges, no fences, no steps, no boats, no people, no animals, no birds. No snow, no cherry blossoms, no plum blossoms, no maple leaves, no autumn colours, no bamboo. The path runs from the lower right into the middle distance and bends out of sight to the left. The sun has just set out of frame to the left: low warm light slants between the grey trunks in long soft bands of apricot and rose across the moss, catching the red of the fallen flowers on the path and the flowers still on the branches. Through small gaps in the canopy the sky is a soft gradated wash from warm rose low down to pale violet above. Apricot, rose, pale violet, deep camellia red, moss green, the dark glossy green of the leaves and soft grey-blue shadow. Japanese shin-hanga woodblock print in the manner of the 1920s-30s revival: flat layered areas of colour, visible woodgrain in the flat passages, softly gradated sky (bokashi), Western perspective and cast light held inside Japanese printmaking. The trees, the leaves and the flowers are drawn as part of the print, in the same flat woodblock manner, never photographic. Calm, no people, no figures. Strong clear difference between the light and dark masses so the image still reads when reduced to a thumbnail. No text, no signature, no seal stamp, no lettering of any kind. No modern objects: no power lines, no utility poles, no electric lamps, no vehicles, no plastic, no road markings. Wide 16:9 landscape. Exposed so that texture is clearly visible everywhere. Shadows are lifted and open, full of visible detail, nothing crushed to pure black. High dynamic range, rich texture even in the darkest areas.
images.visual_review: Warm dusk light across a mossy path with intact fallen red camellias. No people, animals, birds, snow, lettering, seals or buildings seen. Visible flowers have open single-form red petals and yellow stamens rather than rose-like double whorls.
